basics.label: Software Developer · Games & Interactive Apps
basics.summary: Developer with more than 12 years of experience building interactive software: an open-source typing game for children, a streaming app for set-top boxes driven by remote-control focus, real-time WebRTC calling, and a football prediction pool on Ethereum. I enjoy making software that people want to come back to.

highlights: Built tracking for learner and employer enrollments, including automatic re-enrollment when courses change or renew.

Designed and built a new application architecture to replace a legacy system with significant technical debt. Rebuilt rather than patched, because the architectural problems could not be fixed incrementally.
Built and maintained Elixir/Phoenix microservices that consumed operations queued through Kafka and communicated with a Ruby on Rails monolith.
Built the COVID and life insurance purchase flows, then released the life product using LiveView as a multi-step flow.
Built reusable flows for life, quake, COVID, and home insurance, including A/B test variants.
Built experimental projects, including an employee management system (attendance, permissions, surveys, payroll) and a football prediction pool as an Ethereum smart contract.
Led a team building a WebRTC/SIP client, managing issue delegation, stakeholder collaboration, and PR review.

projects.name: TypingSnail
projects.description: Open-source typing game that helps children learn to type: type each letter before the bike splashes the snails.
highlights: 64 levels in 6 worlds, from a single key to fast, mistake-free typing.
Difficulty adapts to each child and is saved between sessions.
Cartoon art drawn with the HTML canvas, sound effects synthesized with Web Audio, and spoken letter names.
Deployed to GitHub Pages with GitHub Actions.
